output.summary: KEP-4331 proposes two separate etcd probes: a liveness probe that checks the local node is up and running, and a readiness probe that checks the cluster is ready to serve traffic. The existing /health probe stays unchanged except for bug fixes. The KEP remains in provisional status.
output.rationale: The single /health probe is used for both liveness and readiness, so it cannot tell whether etcd needs a restart or should stop receiving traffic. The KEP adds separate livez/readyz probes to address this. The sources show the status stayed provisional because the PRR (production readiness review) was not filled in and reviewed when the PR was pushed back.
output.outcome_reason: The KEP was pushed back to provisional because the PRR was not filled in and reviewed, per the reviewer's comments on PR #4338. The sources do not record any later decision.

alternatives.option: Keep using the single /health probe for both liveness and readiness
alternatives.why_not: The readme says it is not Kubernetes API compliant and 'does not differentiate whether etcd needs to restart or stop taking traffic.'

evidence.quote: The current etcd implementation has a single `/health` probe that is used to determine both the liveness and readiness of a node.
It does not differentiate whether etcd needs to restart or stop taking traffic.
Add two separate probes 1. Liveness: the liveness probe would check that the local individual node is up and running, or else restart the node.
pushing back to provisional as PRR was not filled in and reviewed [to pass improved validation]
